summary: Chat streaming stalls mid-generation when concurrent large file upload occurs in same session
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports chat streaming sessions (WebSocket) stall mid-generation (no tokens emitted for >60s) and eventually the client sees a connection close (1006). This consistently reproduces when the same client session uploads a large file (>50MB) to our attachments endpoint while a long-running streaming response is in-flight.

Impact:
- Affects NoteAI Labs production customers using Dedicated cluster in us-west-2.
- Observed on multiple accounts inside NoteAI with high severity (in-progress chat flows drop).
- Business impact: live note-taking sessions are interrupted, user-visible failures for editors using upload+chat simultaneously.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster (dedicated plan), prod us-west-2
- API path: /v1/chat/stream (WebSocket upgrade) and /v1/files/upload in same session token
- SDK: node-redwood v2.3.1 and direct WebSocket clients
- Serving runtime: 2026-02-28 build (kernel v3.4), websocket-proxy v1.9

Steps to reproduce:
1) Open a WebSocket chat stream to /v1/chat/stream and start a long-generation prompt (~1k tokens expected).
2) While generation is in-flight, in the same authenticated session upload a 60MB file using /v1/files/upload.
3) Observe chat stream: token emission halts after ~12s of activity. No error messages are delivered to client. After ~90s, client receives a 1006 close.

Observed behavior:
- Streaming output pauses (silence) mid-token; server shows no 5xx in API gateway logs for the chat request.
- Websocket connection remains ESTABLISHED from the proxy perspective for ~60-120s then unclean close.
- Upload request completes successfully and storage acknowledges file upload.

Expected behavior:
- Upload should not impact in-flight streaming generation. Both requests should make forward progress concurrently.

Logs/Errors/Artifacts:
- Customer-provided client logs show no application-level exception; final close code 1006.
- Gateway metrics: no increased 5xx for chat route; connection count for websocket proxy spikes during upload and CPU on proxy pod increases ~20%.
- Serving runtime logs show a single worker thread blocked in protobuf parsing at the same timestamp as the stall.
- tcpdump on proxy shows continuous POST data for upload while upstream ws packets cease after the stall moment.

Workaround (temporary):
- Ask customers to avoid concurrent large uploads during live streaming sessions.
- If unavoidable, perform uploads on a separate session/token so requests are routed to different backend workers.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Marco Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced locally on a staging dedicated replica with node client. Observed event-loop stall in worker process when large multipart parse occurs concurrently with generation. Attaching staging traces to ticket.

2026-03-11 08:15 - Marco Alvarez (SRE): Hypothesis: synchronous file parsing in the upload handler blocks the event loop thread that's responsible for streaming token flushes to the websocket. This is exacerbated on dedicated nodes when CPU contention is high.

2026-03-11 17:40 - Dev (runtime): Implemented prototype offloading: move multipart parsing to a background worker thread pool and ensure websocket writer uses a dedicated async IO path. Created PR #4287.

investigation_notes: Reproduced using Node SDK v2.3.1 and raw WebSocket client; failure only when same session token used for both concurrent requests.
Strace and async traces show main thread blocked in parse_multipart() inside upload handler; worker uses shared process for websocket flush callbacks.
CPU profile: spike on main thread; websocket writer uses same threadpool due to legacy synchronous flush path.
Proxy observed increased connection multiplexing and head-of-line behavior but proxy not dropping packets; root cause localized to serving runtime process.
Related to internal convo INT-5591 where we previously discussed offloading heavy request parsing; reuse of that design work sped remediation.
resolution: Root cause: synchronous multipart file parsing in upload handler blocked the event-loop thread responsible for websocket token flushes on the serving runtime. Concurrent large uploads in same process led to head-of-line blocking and unclean websocket closures.
Fix: offload multipart parsing to a thread pool and ensure websocket flushes run on a dedicated async IO executor. Implemented in PR #4287.

Rollout: canary deployed 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC (10% traffic), monitored for 12h, then promoted to 100% at 2026-03-12 11:00 UTC across us-west. No further reproductions reported by customer after canary test.

Postmortem action items: 1) Add e2e test for concurrent upload+stream flows; 2) Add telemetry to detect event-loop stalls >200ms on serving runtime; 3) Update SDK docs to recommend separate session tokens for heavy uploads until fully rolled out (temporary).
Status: Resolved. Customer validated fix on canary and confirmed production behavior is restored.
